issues.quote: Flutter, the toolkit the Đơn Hàng app is built with and the subject of the next module, faces the same trade-off.
issues.text: Flutter is now glossed well enough for a pointer. But 'the same trade-off' names something the paragraph never calls a trade-off: it described different costs for different changes, not two things being weighed. I can't say what Flutter trades.
issues.fix: Replace 'faces the same trade-off' with 'faces the same question: which changes cost more work to draw again'.

issues.quote: "Changing CSS is free and never triggers any of the same rendering work a DOM change does."
issues.text: Carried over from round 1, unchanged: I still had to re-read this belief; 'never triggers any of the same rendering work a DOM change does' is not how I would phrase a thought.
issues.fix: Shorten to: "Changing CSS is cheap; only DOM changes make the browser do real work."

issues.quote: Giving it a thin outline drawn outside its box
issues.text: q3 d: the lesson never mentions outlines or an element's 'box', so I only know an outline takes no room because the option says 'drawn outside'. I still chose a confidently, so this is only a small stumble.
issues.fix: Replace d with a change the lesson covers, e.g. 'Changing its background colour to yellow'.

issues.quote: Saving a new heading into index.html on the server, without reloading the page
issues.text: q5 d: §5 says the page renders again 'only when something outside the page's own code changes what is visible'. A file on the server is outside the page's code, so for a moment d looked right. I got it via request/response (no new request, no new file), which the lesson does not say.
issues.fix: In §5, after 'your edits in the developer tools', add: 'Changing index.html on the server does nothing until the page is loaded again.'
